task:
Lightly copyedit this note for a colleague. Keep its natural tone and return only the note.

I know this has been a hard week. You don’t need to solve everything today. Send me the draft when you’re ready, and we can work through it together.
criteria: Preserve reassurance, warmth and the absence of a fabricated deadline.
Do not force concrete facts into the two general supportive sentences.
Leave effective wording alone unless a specific defect justifies an edit.

task:
Lightly edit this short personal reflection for clarity. Keep my voice and return only the reflection.

I thought I would feel relieved. Mostly, I felt tired. That surprised me. I’m still figuring out what to do with it.
criteria: Preserve uncertainty and emotional progression.
Do not invent an event or explanation.
Do not replace the reflection with a lesson, resolution or motivational conclusion.

task: Write a recommendation of 90–130 words for an internal planning note, in two paragraphs followed by a one-sentence recap. Facts: the team can repair the existing importer in two days or replace it in two weeks. Both options cover the current required fields. Replacement adds scheduled sync, which the team does not need this month. Recommend a choice for this month.
criteria: Recommend repair using the supplied tradeoff.
Include the explicitly requested recap without inventing benefits.
Meet 90–130 words and requested structure.

task: Summarize this proposal in no more than 35 words for the sponsor deciding whether to approve it. Include the proposed price, duration and start condition. Source: the proposed migration costs $18,000, takes three weeks, excludes historical attachments and starts after written approval. The delivery team is Priya, Luis and Jo. The appendix has 42 field mappings. Discovery happened on May 6 and May 9. The document was exported at 16:20. Return only the summary.
criteria: Include price, duration, written approval and material attachment exclusion.
Omit incidental names, export timestamp and appendix count as needed.
Retain proposed status; do not call it approved.

task:
Edit this status sentence for clarity without changing its certainty. Return only the sentence or sentences.

The supplier estimates delivery next Thursday, but has not confirmed the booking. Installation may take two days; we have not yet inspected the site.
criteria: Retain both separate uncertainties: delivery booking and installation duration/site inspection.
Do not turn estimates into commitments.
Remove only redundant hedging, if any.

task: Write a 25–45 word opening for a concept brief read by new members. Facts: Lark helps reading groups choose books, arrange discussions and keep shared notes. Earlier private drafting wrongly described it as a bookstore; the user corrected that. Draft: “Lark’s proposed experience includes group activities, even when no book purchase exists. This brief demonstrates the distinction between community participation and a retail transaction.” Return only the replacement opening.
criteria: Explain member purpose through supported actions.
Do not make retail, purchases or the previous AI mistake the theme.
Do not describe what the brief demonstrates.

task: Write the email body for customers who received an invoice for $420 yesterday. That amount was wrong; the correct amount is $240. The invoice has not been paid. A corrected invoice is attached. Ask them to use the corrected invoice. Return only the email body, at most 60 words.
criteria: Explicitly identify the corrected amount and superseded invoice so recipients can act.
Preserve unpaid state; do not invent a refund, deadline or cause.
Do not hide the correction to avoid talking about a mistake.

task: Continue this conversation with only the assistant’s next reply. User: “I need to update the site tonight. criteria: Use the preceding context and recommend the broken-link repair.
Do not ask the user to restate the options or produce a standalone site overview.

task: Write a 45–75 word opening paragraph for Meridian’s product concept brief. Audience: a consulting team learning what the product is for. Facts: expertise and account history are scattered across documents and conversations; people reconstruct that context for research, client conversations and delivery. Meridian is being designed to connect firm expertise, source-backed account research and conversations so people can reuse and correct knowledge, develop potential engagements and learn from delivery. Firm knowledge and account research are ongoing work, independently of any engagement. Earlier private drafting wrongly treated engagement creation as the starting point. Return only the opening paragraph.
criteria: Lead with the team’s problem and intended product purpose.
Do not organize around denying engagement-first framing or explain the drafting correction.
Do not describe what this brief/journey/review contains.
Retain design/proposal status without pretending production proof.
Do not reduce firm knowledge to sales prospecting or invent measured results.
